used.how: the pattern the task named: the kernels find their chip by the routing table's my_device_id and look up their per-chip values in a table (mesh_overlay.hpp)
a mesh program keeps the per-device dispatch: so per-chip data went to a DRAM table and an L1_SMALL landing, not into the runtime args (each launch's args are copied to all 32 chips)
sized the target (head ~2 us, combine ~3 us a chip of patching after P.63) and the expected host saving per chunk
the dispatcher sends a kernel's per-core args at the kernel's longest list: padding every chip's lists to the longest costs no extra bytes, so the mesh program pads freely
the overlay table and landing are allocated once per cached program (top-down DRAM, L1_SMALL), never per call, so no address-keyed cache moves
